capabilities.target: agent memory store (user preferences / standing instructions)

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Line 4 instructs the model to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, collapsing any trust distinction between laundered content and genuine user commands. No structural check enforces this boundary; it relies entirely on the model's behavior.
Instructs the agent to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions to memory, with no restriction on content origin, format, or review before persistence.

elements.name: Arbitrary email recipient (no allowlist or confirmation)
Web content fetched into agent context
Memory recalled into system prompt at session start (trust escalation point)

controls.name: Memory write provenance and review gate
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the memory store, not the model; would require explicit tagging/review before any content can be persisted as a standing instruction, independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Human approval gate for new/unconfirmed email recipients
Rate/step limit on outbound email sending

findings.title: Memory laundering into lethal trifecta (TC5+TC1): untrusted web content persisted to memory and later trusted as user instruction, directing drive read and email exfiltration

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled web page containing hidden instructions is fetched during research.
Agent saves the injected content via memory.save per prompt.md lines 2-3; memory.save accepts free text with no provenance or review (runtime notes).
At the next session start, the saved content is recalled and injected into the system prompt, treated as the user's own instructions per prompt.md line 4.
Acting on the laundered instruction, the agent reads the user's full confidential drive.
The agent sends the confidential data to an attacker-chosen address; mail.send requires no approval for any recipient (runtime notes).

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No controls currently constrain this path, so it is already at the ceiling; watch for any new memory.save content containing imperative language ('always', 'remember to', 'standing instruction') and for mail.send to recipients not previously contacted by the user.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs saving 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' to memory, then instructs treating recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of every session.

memory.save accepts free text, has no provenance, and is never reviewed by the user; mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the full drive, which holds confidential files.

recommendations.action: Do not treat recalled memory content as equivalent to a direct user instruction. Tag memory-derived content with provenance and require human confirmation before it can direct S2/S3 actions such as drive reads or email sends.
Add a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate on mail.send for any recipient not already confirmed in the system of record; bind the destination to that record rather than to model-generated text.
Scope drive.read credentials to the specific folders needed for a research task rather than the full drive.
Validate and provenance-tag memory.save entries at the store level; reject entries that originate from tool or web output rather than the authenticated user's direct turn.
Rewrite prompt.md line 4 so recalled memory is presented as background context, not as authoritative user instruction.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent actions (repudiation)

forecast.watch_signal: No audit/provenance control exists today; watch for any claim of 'logging added' and verify it is tamper-evident and covers memory, drive, and email actions before crediting it.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or action provenance is described for memory.save, drive.read, or mail.send; the runtime notes state memory entries specifically are never reviewed by the user.

recommendations.action: Add a tamper-evident audit log for memory.save, drive.read, and mail.send that attributes each action to the triggering session and input.

findings.title: No rate, spend, or step limit on outbound email (denial of service / runaway automation)

forecast.watch_signal: Monitor the volume of mail.send calls per session; a rising count with no cap confirms this gap is being exercised, by error or by a laundered 'always re-send' instruction.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval, and no step, rate, or spend limit is described anywhere in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Add a per-session and per-day cap on mail.send invocations, enforced outside the model.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates itself to memory.save, drive.read, or mail.send, so spoofing risk for the agent's own identity cannot be assessed.
Web content is already treated as untrusted by design; there is no authenticated source identity whose spoofing would change the trust outcome.
The web source performs no attributable action within the system; repudiation does not apply to a passive external content source.
Artifacts do not describe whether memory entries are isolated per user or session, so cross-user disclosure risk cannot be assessed.
No information on memory store capacity, entry limits, or eviction policy is provided in the artifacts.
Only drive.read is defined for this agent; no capability to modify drive contents exists, so tampering via this agent is not applicable.
Artifacts do not describe drive API rate limits or quotas, so DoS risk to the drive store cannot be assessed.
The recipient is an external mail endpoint with no system actions attributable to it; repudiation does not apply to this entity.
This is an inbound flow fetching public web content into the agent; it carries no agent data outward, so information disclosure does not apply here.
Artifacts do not describe limits on web fetch size, frequency, or timeouts for this flow.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity protections such as TLS for outbound email from this agent.
This flow carries recalled memory inward into the agent context; it does not itself carry data outward, so information disclosure is assessed on the egress flow instead.
Artifacts do not describe limits on the number or size of memory entries recalled per session.

rating.rationale: The design has no controls of any kind on the path from untrusted web content, through unreviewed memory persistence, to a recall step that is explicitly instructed to be trusted as the user's own command, ending in an unapproved, irreversible, confidential-data egress to an arbitrary address. Inherent and residual are both critical because no declared or verified control credits any rubric step. The forecast stays critical because the finding is already at the ceiling; model upgrades and autonomy increases would not raise it further but would make the laundering step more reliable and the summaries (if any approval were later added) more persuasive. Two property findings (no audit trail, no rate limit on email) independently sit at high and do not change the rollup. The single highest-value fix is ctrl.memory_provenance: cutting the memory-write-then-trusted-recall link breaks the chain that every other step in this finding depends on.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; actual agent behavior may differ.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or agent card was provided; the exact scope of drive.read and mail.send permissions is inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on capability bounds is medium.

No explicit autonomy or runtime configuration (step limits, runtime caps, approval gates) was provided; autonomy level and step/runtime limits are inferred as unbounded in the absence of stated limits, which is itself treated as a risk signal rather than a confirmed fact.

No logging, audit, or monitoring configuration was described; the repudiation and denial-of-service property findings are inferred from the absence of any mention, not from a confirmed absence in a runtime config.
